page.layout: One column of running text; marginal notes in the right margin ("Dall." and "pag.109:"). Printed page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: virum puto ) totus hactenus orbis æquo ani-mo tulit, id in Dionysio legi, noli ferre ini-quius: eadem plane ratione probare pos-set eruditus Pearsonius Dionysij scriptaDall. quæ exagitat Dallæus & tanquam spuriapag.109: confodit, genuina illi esse ac legitima, quia hoc in loco in Dionysio simpliciter dixit, æquè ac in Origene: Verum ut nul-lus superstit tergiversandi locus, lucéque meridianâ clarius appareat aliquid huma-ni hîc passum esse doctissimum Vindicia-rum Autorem, forte præ nimio causæ stu-dio, describenda nobis sunt quædam Dallæi verba ex pag. 108. Extant, inquit, quatuor quædam in Canticum Canticorum Homiliæ inter Origenis opera, quas pro vero Origenis fœtu tu tuique Halloixij vulgò ha-betis. Tui certè ex iis adversus nos testimo-nia Origenis nomine laudant, ut Copus, & Coccius; Ac ut cæteros mittam, tu quidem hoc opus Origeni non semel asseris. Nam & ex Homilia tertia locum describis, ut de-monstres Origenem subita Ecclesiæ incremen-ta celebrasse; Et paulò post tria ex eodem opere loca recitas, veluti veras Origenis sen-tentias; & apud multos controversam Ori-genis de sanctissimâ Trinitate Orthodoxiam tribus itidem ex ejus operis Prologo, & Ho-milia tertia petitis testimonijs confirmas, om-nia absurdè & ridiculè, nisi tu hunc scri-

page.notes: The whole Dallæus quotation (from "Extant" to "scri-") is set in italic; the final words "nisi tu hunc scri-" may be roman, which I could not settle with certainty. The "pag.109:" note is followed by a colon as printed. The line-final hyphen in "scri-" is printed and the word continues on the next page. Small italic "Ac" and "&" forms are read as printed.
